title: First-person in Rust: hands hold the weapon, drawn from the camera every frame
note: First-person: draw forearms and hands holding the gun under frame.tag("hands") from the camera in on_draw; a gun without hands floats.
intent: A weapon alone in the lower right of the frame is the classic unfinished first-person view, and judges name it first ([no-hands]). The genex facade has no scene graph and no parenting: the viewmodel is drawn in on_draw from the &Camera the hook is given, as a camera-space offset turned into a world Transform (the camera's basis times the offset), every frame. Draw a pair of gloved forearms and hands holding the gun — rear hand on the grip, front hand cupping it or on the fore-end — under frame.tag("hands") and the gun under frame.tag("weapon"), each under its own frame.id so TAA does not smear them. Build the arms as one modelled GLB (Local Blender: two forearms with sleeves and gloved hands posed on a grip, ~2-6k triangles, real scale) or, as a first pass, from several cubes and spheres per hand; never a single slab. Keep the whole viewmodel within about 0.6 m of the camera and low in the frame (grip around 0.17 right, 0.19 down, 0.45 forward) so it does not reach into walls. Lag it behind the turn (ease a sway offset toward -ctx.look in on_update), bob it from the walking speed the world keeps (never the clock), and kick it back and up on a shot from a decaying world value. Light it like the scene: the viewmodel is lit by the same sun, probes and lights, so a dark interior gives dark hands; give the GLB's gloves a lighter albedo than black and check a capture at low and high.

check.note: First-person: the last frame drew something under frame.tag("hands") and the gun under frame.tag("weapon") — a gun without hands floats.

port: One facet owns the viewmodel (arms and gun) and draws it from the camera in on_draw; the player facet keeps the sway, bob and kick in the world for it to read, and nothing else draws a second gun.

evidence.note: frame.tag, frame.id, frame.model and Transform; the draw hook gets the &Camera.
The three.js recipe fps.hands-in-frame, ported to the genex facade (bodycam B4).
